STEP 1 - Scene: This is a snack, a pile of raw or dry-roasted almonds on a white ceramic dish, photographed from above at a steep angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The dish is a small white triangular/rounded-corner serving dish, roughly 24 cm across its longest undistorted width, so treat it as a side-plate-sized vessel. Area ≈ 3.14 x (12)^2 ≈ 450 cm^2 for a round equivalent; the actual dish is somewhat smaller than a full round, so use about 380 cm^2 of usable surface.

STEP 3 - Items: Almonds (whole, brown-skinned, about 2.5 cm long each). Roughly 75 almonds are visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover about 35% of the dish's usable area, leaving the rest bare.

STEP 5 - Volume: 35% of 380 cm^2 ≈ 133 cm^2 x about 1.5 cm pile height (almonds stacked a couple deep in places) ≈ 200 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole almonds pack loosely, so bulk density is about 0.55 g/ml for nut pieces with gaps. Hmm, whole almonds are denser than cut pieces; use 0.6 g/ml. 200 ml x 0.6 ≈ 120 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are about 579 kcal per 100 g (raw/dry, as plated). 120 g x 5.79 ≈ 695 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 75 almonds at roughly 1.2 g each is about 90 g, so 120 g is a bit high. Adjusting to about 95 g gives about 550 kcal. That is plausible for a generous handful of almonds (roughly 75 nuts), so the final estimate is about 95 g and 550 kcal.
